variants.brief_ru: Узкий высокий корпус, вертикальная пара двигателей у тяжёлых классов, ступенчатые броневые секции и подвижные лопасти с глубокими выемками.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a professional concept design sheet for a PIRATE BOUNTY HUNTER SHIP FAMILY in Freelancer (2003). THREE distinct fighters from one redesigned family, all fully visible: lightweight FIGHTER, medium ELITE, heavy VHEAVY. This is not a freighter sheet. Read the references as actual existing ships, not abstract mood images.

REFERENCE ROLES, ordered:
1. EXACT NATIVE BH GLAZING AND FRAME in multiple views. This is the immutable glazing geometry: one broad shield-shaped central pane that continues over the rounded crown, rounded lower front tip; ONE rounded side pane on each side; two original slanting frame strips. THREE glass panes total. Never split the front with a centre mullion, add horizontal crossbars, add extra windows, turn it into a jet canopy or sphere. All family members share this native cockpit at the same physical scale.
2. Actual bh_pir_elite cockpit close-up. Retain its recognizable rounded upright pilot nose, original frame and glass proportions. Mechanical exterior shoulders may change behind/below it, but do not redesign the cabin. The little yellow-black roof equipment pedestal is optional and should be omitted; it is not part of the glazing.
3. Actual native BH family, flight geometry: lightweight regular fighter on left is only a structural basis (its pirate CMP is absent); pirate Elite and pirate Vheavy are the middle and right. Their existing warm off-white/ochre finish is pirate palette guidance. Learn the slim upright central body, deep side silhouette, sharp fins, distinctive rounded cockpit, attached solid mechanical roots, and forward-reaching wing tips.
4. Actual bh_pir_elite full six-view reference. It is the main ancestry of the new family. Preserve recognizable BH ancestry even where the architecture is reworked.

PRIMARY DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
These are maintained working pirate conversions built by salvage mechanics, with deliberate major hull changes. Pirate character comes from replaceable angular hull sections, different broad armour panel shapes, deep backed recesses, stout integral engine collars, mismatched but well-fitted replacement skins, and exposed useful hinge junctions. No clouds of detail. Do not merely recolour the original. Never turn them into generic modern jets, cargo trucks, capital ships or literal fish.
Fish-theme ancestry is Piranha / Barracuda / Hammerhead; express it through mass proportions, blade planes and the relationship between a blunt upright head and tapered body. No animal mouths, teeth, eyes, gills, fins made of flesh, horns, skulls or demonic decoration.
Use clear hard-surface silhouettes, planar section changes and a few meaningful medium-size recesses. Detail richness comparable to native Freelancer, moderately more depth at joints and large recesses. No exposed tubes, wires, external skeletons, open truss cages, random diagonal braces, tiny rivet forests, serrated sawteeth or ornamental spikes. Necessary attached solid hinges are permitted.
Symmetric main construction; local repair patches may vary. Light service wear only, no stripped wrecks or flaky rust everywhere. Warm ivory / weathered light alloy panels, desaturated ochre and burnt-brown major structural bands, dark brown backed recesses and dark teal original glazing. No bright logos, flags or lettering on hull.
Pilot cabin is small relative to the complete fighter, native scale and shape; never inflate it. Keep close to original fighter-class dimensions. The lightweight must be noticeably slimmer and simpler than the heavy, not the same ship at three zoom levels. The ELITE is the central design anchor.

MECHANICAL INTENT:
All drawings show the same EXTENDED FLIGHT pose. Keep articulated outer parts visually separate at meaningful hinge/sliding roots. Reserve a clear closed two-leaf cargo hatch on the top deck BEHIND the dorsal fin base, not half the ship. Native BH pirate top fin retracts down, lower fin retracts up/back; lateral wing assembly rotates down while its support slides back/up. The new concept must leave plausible external room for these movements. Do not draw invented motion arrows or claim validated kinematics. Do not bridge the hatch with fixed armour or bury the engine outlets. Recesses and gaps have solid backing.
Engine count, placement, cockpit, wing roots and fin direction MUST agree between front, rear and side views of each row. Rear view must show the WHOLE ship including its bow and wing extremities, not an isolated stern.

SHEET LAYOUT:
Landscape 3:2, clean pale warm-grey studio background, crisp shaded industrial concept illustration. THREE rows, each with THREE views: large whole-ship FRONT 3/4, large whole-ship REAR 3/4, readable small SIDE profile. Nine ship drawings total, generous separation and complete silhouettes. Top row FIGHTER; middle ELITE; bottom VHEAVY. Use consistent cockpit scale across the rows so classes read honestly, not equal-sized enlarged clones. Reserve enough pixels to see the original glass boundaries. Neutral lighting; no cinematic scene, humans, weapons attached, explosions, isolated parts, beauty-shot cropping or irrelevant captions.
Column labels exactly FRONT 3/4, REAR 3/4, SIDE. Row labels exactly FIGHTER, ELITE, VHEAVY.

DESIGN DIRECTION — BHP01 / STEPPED KEEL:
A strongly VERTICAL, narrow pirate family. Keep the original BH upright cockpit and deep narrow trunk. Rebuild the trunk aft of the cockpit as three connected angular steps with broad flush replacement panels. A dark closed longitudinal recess is carved into each flank, backed and interrupted by two stout integral joints, not an exposed frame. Top fin is a broad clean stepped blade retracting into a low solid cassette ahead of the small hatch. Bottom fin is a shorter heavy angular keel with one purposeful rectangular recess; both preserve sharp native BH blade character.
FIGHTER: smallest narrow knife-like ship, ONE central rear engine, no long lateral wings. Small low cheek stubs only. An offset stepped top blade and short ventral blade give the family signature. Cabin is the original cabin, not a new shape.
ELITE: TWO rear engines STACKED VERTICALLY, lower unit slightly forward. Two distinct broad engine collars attach to the deep trunk. Pair of medium forward-swept folding wings at the low original BH shoulder level: thick closed root shoe, thinner blade, ONE deep rectangular step/notch in the trailing edge, pointed forward outer tips. The top and lower fins are stepped plates with capped ends, not hooks or fangs.
VHEAVY: the same-size native cabin, a somewhat deeper reinforced rear trunk, TWO engines still vertically stacked. Wings gain a second broad outer articulated plate and an angular inset shoulder; reinforce shape with large connected sections instead of adding many spikes. Dorsal and ventral blade profiles differ from Elite by one extra large step, not by a forest of fins.
The major silhouette should be upright, compact, modular and recognizably BH, visibly different from the original thin continuous wing planes.
Title exactly "BH PIRATE FAMILY / BHP01".

variants.brief_ru: Родная вертикальная кабина и узкий киль переходят в расширенную корму; два двигателя тяжёлых классов разведены по бокам, крылья короче и состоят из двух цельных лопастей.

Wing roots sit low and forward of the engine shoulders. Each wing has TWO connected broad angular blades with a hinge seam: short outward root plate, forward-reaching outer plate, a clean step in the rear outline. They are modest in span and visually capable of folding down, never a single huge manta wing. Preserve a clear top cargo hatch between the dorsal base and engine shoulders.

Root shoulders become double-depth with wide dark backed triangular recesses; outer wing plates have longer forward tips and one additional inset cut, not more fin count. Lower keel is deeper but short. Keep the original same-size native cockpit and narrow forebody; this is a heavier fighter, not a large cargo volume.
Use fitted spare armour with broad ivory shapes separated by brown structural seams. The redesign should be recognizable in flat silhouette and from the rear: narrow original BH face, solid widened engine stern, compact split folding wings. No exposed bars, pipes or wingtip engines.
Title exactly "BH PIRATE FAMILY / BHP02".
